Yazyev, Andras Kis</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Asmund Ottesen, Shun Feng, Edoardo Lopriore, et al.</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Experimental study on exciton control and transport in few-layer 2D heterostructures.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#2Dmaterials</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#heterostructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#excitons</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#ferroelectricity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#opticalspectroscopy</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arxiv-logo-fb.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons.       <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26160</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Lucien Jezequel, Christophe Mora</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Unified theoretical framework for topological gapless modes in Dirac semimetals and TIs.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topological</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Diracsemimetal</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topologicalinsulator</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#bandstructure</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2611.26160v1/Figure/qwz_reduction.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Topologically protected gapless modes emerge across multiple platforms, ranging from nodes in the band structure to boundary states in topologically non-trivial insulators, with each case governed by distinct topological classifications and invariants. Here, we generalize the spectral localizer method to establish a unified framework for topological gapless modes. The spectral localizer reduces the original Hamiltonian to a zero-dimensional operator by recursively applying quantum confining operators, which need not be diagonal in either position or momentum space, as previously assumed. We illustrate our approach using lattice models in symmetry classes A, AIII, AII, and D, verifying that topological transitions coincide with a vanishing gap in the spectral localizer operator.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[7] Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26616</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Vladimir Juri\v{c}i\'c, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory on fractional charge at dislocations in topological crystals, relevant for Weyl semimetals.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topological</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Weylsemimetal</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#crystaldefects</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2611.26616v1/response_overview.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">

      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17591</link>

      <title>[7] Unusual critical currents in quasi-one-dimensional superconducting aluminum two-width structures in a magnetic field (V.I. Kuznetsov, O.V. Trofimov, Physica B)</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27881</link>

In high fields, the switching current is due to equilibrium fluctuations of the order parameter.</p></description>

      <title>[8] Nonuniform superconducting states from Majorana flat bands (Phys. Rev. B)</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03859</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Sushanth Varada, Aksel Kobia{\l}ka, Ankita Bhattacharya, Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer</p><p><b>Published as:</b> Phys. Rev. B <a href='https://doi.org/10.1103/q8w8-y7fk'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical study of nonuniform superconducting states arising from Majorana flat bands in topological superconductors.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Majorana</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topologicalsuperconductor</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#flatband</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2605.03859v2/Experimental_setup_schematic.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Zero-energy flat bands within the superconducting gap can give rise to competing ordered phases. We investigate such phases in topological superconductors based on the magnetic adatom platform hosting a flat band of Majorana edge states. Our self-consistent calculations of the superconducting order parameter show the emergence of both a pair density wave with edge-localized amplitude modulations, often a bond wave order, and a phase crystal characterized by longer-wavelength edge-localized phase modulations. Both these states lower the free energy by gapping out the Majorana flat band, but use different mechanisms tied to the underlying topology. In fact, at zero temperature the uniform superconducting solution with Majorana flat band never survives.       <title>[9] Emergence and Detection of Surface altermagnetism in KV2Se2O</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03551</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Alexander Mook, Jairo Sinova</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Colin Lange, et al.</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 9/10</span> <b>A_MUST_READ</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Links altermagnetism to photoemission spectroscopy in a real material, highly relevant to user's interests.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#altermagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#photoemission</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#electronicstructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#realmaterial</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03551v2/surface_states.001.jpeg' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We demonstrate the recent concept of emergent surface altermagnetism through its unique signatures in KV$_2$Se$_2$O. We show that for bulk antiferromagnetically ordered KV$_2$Se$_2$O, the (001) surface exhibits $d$-wave altermagnetism. Our results fully explain the recent seemingly contradicgting experimental evidence, independently showing both an antiferromagnetically ordered bulk from neutron diffraction, and $d$-wave spin splitting from photoemission spectroscopy. To fully verify this conecept, we predict, as a key experimental signature, a large nonlinear Edelstein response, which is localized at the surface, and follows the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry.       <title>[7] Gauge invariance, collective modes, and the justification of normal-state subtraction in Dirac superconductors (J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.)</title>

Jpn. <a href='https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.95.124705'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical justification of normal-state subtraction for electromagnetic response in Dirac superconductors, relevant to experiment interpretation.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Diracmaterials</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#electromagneticresponse</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> In Dirac superconductors, the unbounded spectrum of low-energy Dirac models is known to give rise to unphysical interband contributions from deep-lying states to the electromagnetic response. To eliminate these contributions, normal-state subtraction (NSS), in which the normal-state response is subtracted from the superconducting-state response, has been widely employed. However, the relation between NSS and a gauge-invariant electromagnetic response, particularly the role of the vertex correction required by the Ward identity, has remained unclear. In this work, we consider a massive-Dirac model with $s$-wave pairing and analytically investigate the electromagnetic response at zero temperature by solving the Bethe--Salpeter equation and incorporating the collective-mode contribution to the electromagnetic vertex. We show that, in the static long-wavelength limit, the vertex correction exactly cancels the bare longitudinal response with NSS, yielding the vanishing longitudinal response required by gauge invariance. In contrast, the transverse component of the vertex correction vanishes in the long-wavelength limit, so that the gauge-invariant Meissner weight coincides with that obtained from the bare transverse response with NSS. Moreover, within the class of isotropic and analytic UV regularization terms, we show that gauge invariance uniquely fixes the regularization term in the static long-wavelength limit to the value prescribed by NSS. Our results thus provide a microscopic justification for NSS.</p></description>

Jpn. <a href='https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.95.124705'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical justification of normal-state subtraction for electromagnetic response in Dirac superconductors, relevant to experiment interpretation.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Diracmaterials</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#electromagneticresponse</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> In Dirac superconductors, the unbounded spectrum of low-energy Dirac models is known to give rise to unphysical interband contributions from deep-lying states to the electromagnetic response. To eliminate these contributions, normal-state subtraction (NSS), in which the normal-state response is subtracted from the superconducting-state response, has been widely employed. However, the relation between NSS and a gauge-invariant electromagnetic response, particularly the role of the vertex correction required by the Ward identity, has remained unclear. In this work, we consider a massive-Dirac model with $s$-wave pairing and analytically investigate the electromagnetic response at zero temperature by solving the Bethe--Salpeter equation and incorporating the collective-mode contribution to the electromagnetic vertex. We show that, in the static long-wavelength limit, the vertex correction exactly cancels the bare longitudinal response with NSS, yielding the vanishing longitudinal response required by gauge invariance. In contrast, the transverse component of the vertex correction vanishes in the long-wavelength limit, so that the gauge-invariant Meissner weight coincides with that obtained from the bare transverse response with NSS. Moreover, within the class of isotropic and analytic UV regularization terms, we show that gauge invariance uniquely fixes the regularization term in the static long-wavelength limit to the value prescribed by NSS. Our results thus provide a microscopic justification for NSS.</p></content:encoded></item>

      <title>[7] Magnetic field induced modulation of heat transport in CrPS4 probed by TaIrTe4 transverse Seebeck thermometry</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19833</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Joseph Barker, Bart J. van Wees</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Krishnaraajan Sundararajan, Sergio Alvarruiz, C\'edric A. <item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[7] Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics (Matter & Light)</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19157</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Vaclav D\v{e}di\v{c}, Lorenzo Dominici</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Adriano Cola, Antonio Valletta, Isabella Farella, Vaclav D\v{e}di\v{c}, Lorenzo Dominici</p><p><b>Published as:</b> Matter &amp; Light <a href='https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matlit.2026.100141'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Novel experimental technique for visualizing charge dynamics and transport in various condensed-matter materials.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#methodology</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#transport</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#experimentaltechnique</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#semiconductor</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#low-dimensionalmaterials</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2607.19157v2/fig1.jpg' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. Furthermore, the internal conduction- and displacement-current profiles are obtained from the electric-field dynamics and shown to be consistent with the externally measured current transients. Demonstrated in CdTe radiation detectors with micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution, CDPI is applicable to materials exhibiting a measurable Pockels effect, including electro-optic semiconductors, oxides, halide perovskites, organic materials, and emerging low-dimensional systems, providing a platform to investigate charge transport across optoelectronics.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[7] Exact fermionic decay length and Majorana localization in the sign-alternating kagom\'e Ising model</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26529</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Hrachya Babujian, Ara SEdrakyan</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Shahane Khachatryan, Hrachya Babujian, Ara SEdrakyan</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Kagome lattice study with topological/Majorana implications, tangentially relevant to current interests.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#kagome</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topological</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Majorana</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We derive an exact fermionic decay length for the sign-alternating kagom\'e Ising model at fixed transverse momentum $p=\pi/2$. Writing $x=\tanh K_1$, $y=\tanh K_2$, and $z=\tanh K_3$ for the three dimensionless couplings, the inverse length per lattice cell is $\xi_{\rm f}^{-1}=|\ln(U/|V|)|$, where $U=(1-x^2)(1+y^2z^2)$ and $V=(1+x^2)(y^2-z^2)$. The length diverges at $U=|V|$, with the sign of $V$ selecting one of two classical critical branches. In a simultaneous strong- and weak-bond scaling, these branches become the gap-closing conditions at momenta $0$ and $\pi$ of the transverse-field Ising chain obtained from the row transfer matrix. On the topological side, the classical decay length tends to the localization length of a Majorana end mode of the Jordan--Wigner fermion chain. We also prove that the regular strong-bond Yang--Baxter family cannot be continued to the finite-coupling interior within the fixed-basis ansatz with one vanishing bond direction.</p></description>

    <content:encoded><p><b>Last authors:</b> Hrachya Babujian, Ara SEdrakyan</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Shahane Khachatryan, Hrachya Babujian, Ara SEdrakyan</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Kagome lattice study with topological/Majorana implications, tangentially relevant to current interests.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#kagome</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topological</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Majorana</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We derive an exact fermionic decay length for the sign-alternating kagom\'e Ising model at fixed transverse momentum $p=\pi/2$. Writing $x=\tanh K_1$, $y=\tanh K_2$, and $z=\tanh K_3$ for the three dimensionless couplings, the inverse length per lattice cell is $\xi_{\rm f}^{-1}=|\ln(U/|V|)|$, where $U=(1-x^2)(1+y^2z^2)$ and $V=(1+x^2)(y^2-z^2)$. The length diverges at $U=|V|$, with the sign of $V$ selecting one of two classical critical branches. In a simultaneous strong- and weak-bond scaling, these branches become the gap-closing conditions at momenta $0$ and $\pi$ of the transverse-field Ising chain obtained from the row transfer matrix. On the topological side, the classical decay length tends to the localization length of a Majorana end mode of the Jordan--Wigner fermion chain. We also prove that the regular strong-bond Yang--Baxter family cannot be continued to the finite-coupling interior within the fixed-basis ansatz with one vanishing bond direction.</p></content:encoded></item>

Besides orbital phase transitions, it can give rise to a plethora of emergent phenomena, from exotic magnetic states, orbital-liquid phases, hidden order and much more. Yet, to identify real systems in which orbital-ordering arises purely from the Kugel-Khomskii mechanism has been a challenge. The first obstacle was that ions with orbital degrees of freedom are also of the Jahn-Teller kind. This poses a chicken-and-egg problem: electronic ordering can give rise to distortions and distortions can give rise to orbital ordering. This problem was eventually solved, showing that the two effects can be indeed disentangled. From this the next obstacle emerged: lattice distortions are very efficient in freezing orbital fluctuations, hampering the effects of orbital super-exchange. Thus, in most systems, orbital ordering occurs well above T KK , the critical temperature at which super-exchange can drive it. Representative Kugel-Khomskii systems were recently identified, however. The understanding gained provides guidelines for finding Kugel-Khomskii materials. It also indicates that experimental signatures of the Kugel-Khomskii mechanism should be mostly searched via the primary effect, electronic and magnetic properties, rather than the secondary effect, lattice distortions.</p></description><content:encoded><p><b>Last authors:</b> Erik Koch, Eva Pavarini</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 5/10</span> <b>C_MAYBE</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Discussion of orbital-ordering mechanisms in real correlated systems.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#orbital-physics</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#correlated-electrons</span></p><p><img src='https://media.springernature.com/m685/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41535-026-00942-z/MediaObjects/41535_2026_942_Fig1_HTML.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> The Kugel-Khomskii super-exchange mechanism for orbital ordering is a pillar of orbital physics. Besides orbital phase transitions, it can give rise to a plethora of emergent phenomena, from exotic magnetic states, orbital-liquid phases, hidden order and much more. Yet, to identify real systems in which orbital-ordering arises purely from the Kugel-Khomskii mechanism has been a challenge. The first obstacle was that ions with orbital degrees of freedom are also of the Jahn-Teller kind. This poses a chicken-and-egg problem: electronic ordering can give rise to distortions and distortions can give rise to orbital ordering. This problem was eventually solved, showing that the two effects can be indeed disentangled. From this the next obstacle emerged: lattice distortions are very efficient in freezing orbital fluctuations, hampering the effects of orbital super-exchange. Thus, in most systems, orbital ordering occurs well above T KK , the critical temperature at which super-exchange can drive it. Knupfer, B. Büchner</p><p><b>Authors:</b> A. Koitzsch, T. Klaproth, O. Janson, A. A. Popov, M. Knupfer, B. Büchner</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Strain control of interactions in a prominent Kitaev candidate material.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#experiment</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#RuCl3</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Kitaev</span></p><p><img src='https://media.springernature.com/m685/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41535-026-00939-8/MediaObjects/41535_2026_939_Fig1_HTML.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We have studied optical transmission spectra of exfoliated α -RuCl 3 flakes as a function of thickness and strain.
